head--scalp.name: Scalp
head--scalp.summary: Occipitofrontalis and its neighbour, joined by the epicranial aponeurosis. All muscles of facial expression are supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII).

head--eyelids.name: Around the eye
head--eyelids.summary: Muscles that close the eyelids and move the eyebrows.

head--nose.name: Around the nose
head--nose.summary: Small muscles that flare or narrow the nostrils.

head--mouth.name: Around the mouth
head--mouth.summary: The largest group of facial muscles: they open, close and shape the lips and cheeks.

head--mastication.name: Muscles of mastication
head--mastication.summary: The chewing muscles that move the mandible at the temporomandibular joint. All supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3).

head--eye-muscles.name: Eye muscles
head--eye-muscles.summary: Two of the extraocular muscles are in the model. Remember LR6 SO4: lateral rectus by CN VI, superior oblique by CN IV, the rest by CN III.

head--tongue.name: Tongue
head--tongue.summary: Extrinsic tongue muscles, supplied by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

neck--superficial.name: Superficial neck
neck--superficial.summary: Platysma in the skin and sternocleidomastoid, which divides the neck into its anterior and posterior triangles.

neck--suprahyoid.name: Suprahyoid muscles
neck--suprahyoid.summary: Above the hyoid: they raise the hyoid for swallowing or, with the hyoid fixed, open the jaw.

neck--infrahyoid.name: Infrahyoid muscles
neck--infrahyoid.summary: The strap muscles below the hyoid. They pull the hyoid and larynx down; mostly supplied by the ansa cervicalis (C1–C3).

neck--scalenes.name: Scalenes
neck--scalenes.summary: Lateral neck muscles running to the first two ribs. The brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass between the anterior and middle scalenes.

neck--prevertebral.name: Prevertebral muscles
neck--prevertebral.summary: Deep neck flexors lying on the front of the cervical spine.

frontalis.name: Frontalis (frontal belly of occipitofrontalis)
frontalis.insertion: Skin and fascia of the forehead and eyebrows.
frontalis.actionText: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead (surprise).
frontalis.note: Has no bony attachment of its own: it moves skin over the frontal bone.

occipitalis.name: Occipitalis (occipital belly of occipitofrontalis)
occipitalis.origin: Lateral two-thirds of the superior nuchal line and the mastoid process.

temporoparietalis.insertion: Lateral border of the epicranial aponeurosis.
temporoparietalis.actionText: Tightens the scalp and slightly raises the ear. Variable in size.

orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.name: Orbicularis oculi, orbital part
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.origin: Nasal part of the frontal bone, frontal process of the maxilla and the medial palpebral ligament.
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.insertion: Skin around the orbit, in a ring back to the origin.
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.nerveNote: Facial nerve, temporal and zygomatic branches
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.actionText: Closes the eyelids tightly (squeezing the eyes shut, squinting).
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.note: Inability to close the eye on one side is a key sign of facial nerve palsy (for example Bell's palsy).

palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.name: Orbicularis oculi, palpebral part
palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.insertion: Lateral palpebral raphe, within the eyelids.
palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.nerveNote: Facial nerve, temporal and zygomatic branches
palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.actionText: Closes the eyelids gently, as in blinking and sleep.

corrugator-supercilii.origin: Medial end of the superciliary arch of the frontal bone.
corrugator-supercilii.insertion: Skin above the middle of the eyebrow.
corrugator-supercilii.actionText: Draws the eyebrows down and together, making vertical frown lines.

procerus.origin: Fascia over the nasal bone and upper nasal cartilage.
procerus.nerveNote: Facial nerve, temporal and buccal branches
procerus.actionText: Pulls the inner eyebrows down and wrinkles the bridge of the nose.

nasalis.origin: Maxilla above the incisor and canine teeth.
nasalis.insertion: Nasal cartilages and the skin of the nose.
nasalis.actionText: Its transverse part narrows the nostrils; its alar part flares them.

depressor-septi-nasi.origin: Incisive fossa of the maxilla, above the central incisor.
depressor-septi-nasi.insertion: Mobile part of the nasal septum.
depressor-septi-nasi.actionText: Pulls the nasal septum down and narrows the nostrils.

levator-nasolabialis.name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
levator-nasolabialis.insertion: Alar cartilage of the nose and the upper lip.
levator-nasolabialis.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
levator-nasolabialis.actionText: Elevates the upper lip and flares the nostril (a snarl).

orbicularis-oris.origin: Maxilla and mandible near the midline, and the modiolus at each corner of the mouth.
orbicularis-oris.insertion: Skin and mucous membrane of the lips.
orbicularis-oris.nerveNote: Facial nerve, buccal and marginal mandibular branches
orbicularis-oris.actionText: Closes the lips and purses or protrudes them (whistling, kissing).

bucinator.name: Buccinator
bucinator.origin: Alveolar processes of the maxilla and mandible opposite the molars, and the pterygomandibular raphe.
bucinator.insertion: Angle of the mouth, blending with orbicularis oris.
bucinator.actionText: Presses the cheek against the teeth, keeping food between them when chewing; helps blow and whistle.
bucinator.note: Supplied by the facial nerve, not by the buccal branch of the trigeminal nerve (which only carries sensation).

zygomaticus-major.origin: Lateral surface of the zygomatic bone.
zygomaticus-major.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
zygomaticus-major.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
zygomaticus-major.actionText: Draws the angle of the mouth up and out: the smiling muscle.

zygomaticus-minor.origin: Anterior surface of the zygomatic bone.
zygomaticus-minor.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches

levator-labii-superioris.insertion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip.
levator-labii-superioris.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
levator-labii-superioris.actionText: Elevates and everts the upper lip.

levator-anguli-oris.origin: Canine fossa of the maxilla, below the infraorbital foramen.
levator-anguli-oris.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
levator-anguli-oris.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
levator-anguli-oris.actionText: Elevates the angle of the mouth.

risorius.origin: Parotid fascia and the skin over the masseter.
risorius.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
risorius.actionText: Pulls the angle of the mouth straight out to the side (a grimace).

depressor-anguli-oris.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
depressor-anguli-oris.actionText: Pulls the angle of the mouth down (frowning, sadness).

depressor-labii-inferioris.insertion: Skin and muscle of the lower lip.
depressor-labii-inferioris.actionText: Pulls the lower lip down and to the side.

mentalis.actionText: Raises and protrudes the lower lip and wrinkles the chin (pouting).

superficial-part-of-masseter.name: Masseter, superficial part
superficial-part-of-masseter.origin: Lower border of the front two-thirds of the zygomatic arch and the zygomatic process of the maxilla.
superficial-part-of-masseter.insertion: Angle and lower lateral surface of the ramus of the mandible.
superficial-part-of-masseter.nerveNote: Masseteric nerve, from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3)
superficial-part-of-masseter.actionText: Elevates the mandible (closes the jaw) and helps protrude it.
superficial-part-of-masseter.note: Clench your teeth and you can feel it bulge at the angle of the jaw.

deep-part-of-masseter.name: Masseter, deep part
deep-part-of-masseter.origin: Inner surface and back third of the zygomatic arch.
deep-part-of-masseter.insertion: Upper lateral ramus and the coronoid process of the mandible.
deep-part-of-masseter.actionText: Elevates the mandible and helps retract it.

temporalis.origin: Floor of the temporal fossa and the deep surface of the temporal fascia.
temporalis.insertion: Coronoid process and the front of the ramus of the mandible.
temporalis.nerveNote: Deep temporal nerves, from CN V3
temporalis.actionText: Elevates the mandible; its horizontal back fibres retract it.

medial-pterygoid.origin: Medial surface of the lateral pterygoid plate (sphenoid), the palatine bone and the tuberosity of the maxilla.
medial-pterygoid.insertion: Medial surface of the ramus of the mandible near the angle.
medial-pterygoid.nerveNote: Nerve to medial pterygoid, from CN V3
medial-pterygoid.actionText: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; acting with the opposite side's lateral pterygoid it grinds the jaw from side to side.

superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.name: Lateral pterygoid, superior head
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.origin: Infratemporal surface of the greater wing of the sphenoid.
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.insertion: Articular disc and capsule of the temporomandibular joint and the neck of the mandible.
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.nerveNote: Nerve to lateral pterygoid, from CN V3
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.actionText: Steadies the disc and condyle as the jaw closes; helps protrude the mandible.

inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.name: Lateral pterygoid, inferior head
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate.
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.insertion: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the mandible.
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.nerveNote: Nerve to lateral pterygoid, from CN V3
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.actionText: Pulls the condyle forward to protrude the mandible and to open the mouth wide; one side swings the jaw to the opposite side.
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.note: The only muscle of mastication that helps open the jaw.

lateral-rectus.origin: Common tendinous ring at the back of the orbit.
lateral-rectus.insertion: Sclera on the lateral side of the eyeball.
lateral-rectus.note: Abducens palsy leaves the eye turned inward and causes double vision on looking to that side.

superior-oblique.origin: Body of the sphenoid above the optic canal.
superior-oblique.insertion: Sclera at the back of the upper lateral eyeball, after passing through the trochlea.
superior-oblique.actionText: Depresses the eye when it is turned inward (looking down toward the nose), and rotates it inward (intorsion).
superior-oblique.note: Trochlear palsy makes walking downstairs and reading difficult; patients tilt the head away from the affected side.

genioglossus.origin: Superior mental spine on the inner surface of the mandible.
genioglossus.insertion: Whole length of the tongue's underside and the body of the hyoid.
genioglossus.actionText: Protrudes the tongue and depresses its centre.
genioglossus.note: With a hypoglossal nerve lesion, the protruded tongue points toward the weak side.

hyoglossus.origin: Body and greater horn of the hyoid.
hyoglossus.insertion: Side and underside of the tongue.

platysma.origin: Fascia over the upper pectoralis major and deltoid.
platysma.insertion: Lower border of the mandible, the skin of the lower face and the angle of the mouth.
platysma.actionText: Tenses the skin of the neck and draws the corners of the mouth and the mandible down (a strained grimace).

sternocleidomastoid.origin: Sternal head: front of the manubrium. Clavicular head: upper surface of the medial third of the clavicle.
sternocleidomastoid.insertion: Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral half of the superior nuchal line.
sternocleidomastoid.nerveNote: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with proprioceptive fibres from C2–C3
sternocleidomastoid.actionText: One side bends the neck to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side. Both sides flex the neck (and extend the head on the neck) and lift the sternum in forced inspiration.
sternocleidomastoid.note: The right SCM turns the face to the left. A shortened SCM in infants causes torticollis.

anterior-belly-of-digastric.name: Digastric, anterior belly
anterior-belly-of-digastric.origin: Digastric fossa on the inner lower border of the mandible.
anterior-belly-of-digastric.insertion: Intermediate tendon, held to the hyoid by a fibrous sling.
anterior-belly-of-digastric.nerveNote: Nerve to mylohyoid, from CN V3
anterior-belly-of-digastric.actionText: Elevates the hyoid; with the hyoid fixed, opens the jaw.
anterior-belly-of-digastric.note: Its two bellies have different nerves because they develop from different pharyngeal arches.

posterior-belly-of-digastric.name: Digastric, posterior belly
posterior-belly-of-digastric.origin: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone.
posterior-belly-of-digastric.insertion: Intermediate tendon, held to the hyoid by a fibrous sling.
posterior-belly-of-digastric.actionText: Elevates and retracts the hyoid; helps open the jaw.

stylohyoid.origin: Styloid process of the temporal bone.
stylohyoid.actionText: Elevates and retracts the hyoid, lengthening the floor of the mouth during swallowing.

mylohyoid.origin: Mylohyoid line on the inner surface of the mandible.
mylohyoid.insertion: Midline raphe and the body of the hyoid.
mylohyoid.nerveNote: Nerve to mylohyoid, from CN V3
mylohyoid.actionText: Forms the floor of the mouth; elevates the hyoid, floor of the mouth and tongue in swallowing; helps open the jaw.

geniohyoid.origin: Inferior mental spine of the mandible.
geniohyoid.actionText: Pulls the hyoid up and forward; with the hyoid fixed, helps open the jaw.

sternohyoid.origin: Back of the manubrium and the medial end of the clavicle.

omohyoid.origin: Upper border of the scapula near the suprascapular notch.
omohyoid.insertion: Lower border of the body of the hyoid.
omohyoid.actionText: Depresses and steadies the hyoid; has two bellies joined by an intermediate tendon tethered to the clavicle.

sternothyroid.insertion: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
sternothyroid.actionText: Depresses the larynx (and with it the hyoid).

thyrohyoid.origin: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
thyrohyoid.insertion: Lower border of the body and greater horn of the hyoid.
thyrohyoid.actionText: Depresses the hyoid; with the hyoid fixed, raises the larynx during swallowing.

scalenus-anterior.name: Anterior scalene
scalenus-anterior.origin: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3–C6.
scalenus-anterior.insertion: Scalene tubercle of the first rib.
scalenus-anterior.actionText: Elevates the first rib in forced inspiration; bends the neck to the same side and helps flex it.
scalenus-anterior.note: Tight scalenes can compress the brachial plexus (thoracic outlet syndrome).

scalenus-medius.name: Middle scalene
scalenus-medius.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C2–C7.
scalenus-medius.insertion: Upper surface of the first rib behind the groove for the subclavian artery.
scalenus-medius.actionText: Elevates the first rib and bends the neck to the same side.

scalenus-posterior.name: Posterior scalene
scalenus-posterior.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C4–C6.
scalenus-posterior.insertion: Outer surface of the second rib.
scalenus-posterior.actionText: Elevates the second rib and bends the neck to the same side.

longus-colli.origin: Bodies of C5–T3 and the transverse processes of C3–C5.
longus-colli.insertion: Anterior tubercle of the atlas, the bodies of C2–C4 and the transverse processes of C5–C6.
longus-colli.actionText: Flexes the neck and helps bend and rotate it; important for holding the cervical spine stable.
longus-colli.note: A deep neck flexor often retrained after whiplash and in neck pain (the cranio-cervical flexion test).

longus-capitis.origin: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3–C6.
longus-capitis.insertion: Basilar part of the occipital bone.
longus-capitis.actionText: Flexes the head on the neck.

rectus-anterior-capitis.name: Rectus capitis anterior
rectus-anterior-capitis.origin: Front of the lateral mass of the atlas.
rectus-anterior-capitis.insertion: Base of the occipital bone in front of the condyle.
rectus-anterior-capitis.actionText: Flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

rectus-lateralis-capitis.name: Rectus capitis lateralis
rectus-lateralis-capitis.insertion: Jugular process of the occipital bone.
rectus-lateralis-capitis.actionText: Bends the head to the same side and steadies it.
